messages:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: streaming-ingest latency spike detected. p95=420ms p99=980ms (baseline p95~120ms). KV cache eviction rate jumped to ~32k/min in the last 3m, slab fragmentation increasing. Auto-remediate hasn't stabilized.

jules: paging oncall — looks like a cache pressure event. tagging SREs.

maya: I'm on it, pulling dashboards. Cache hit rate fell from 98% -> 86% over last 4m. Prefill vs decode timing skewed: prefill queue depth down, decode queue backlog up.

aj: logs showing repeated errors: "kv: prefill: failed to allocate slab" and a lot of "decode queue full" warnings. Looks like prefill thrashing followed by decode stalls.

ben: quick mitigation options: 1) throttle prefill workers to reduce churn, 2) raise cache waterline (temporarily) to reduce eviction frequency, 3) enable streaming-degraded-mode to avoid long tail blocking. Any preference for 1st action?

maya: I'll reduce prefill parallelism first, small blast. Doing on prod umbrella.

maya: running command now:
```bash
# reduce prefill worker count across inference pods
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/inference-service PREFILL_WORKERS=2
``` 

deploy-bot: config change applied to 6 pods (rolling)

aj: seeing immediate effect — eviction rate down to ~8k/min within 30s, decode queue depth decreasing.

ben: good. If that holds we should still prepare to toggle degraded streaming to avoid p99 tail stalls for long sequences.

maya: toggling degraded mode and bumping waterline to 95% now:
```json
{"feature.streaming_degraded": true, "kv.cache.waterline": 0.95}
```

deploy-bot: feature flags updated: streaming_degraded=true, kv.cache.waterline=0.95

maya: metrics update: p95 down to ~180ms, p99 ~420ms. Eviction rate ~3.8k/min. Still above baseline but stable. Customer impact estimate: ~0.9% of streaming sessions experienced stalls >5s during the peak window. SLO p99 breach for ~5 minutes on ingest route.

jules: good containment. I'll prepare a short incident summary for handoff. I need to step out in 15m — oncall-ryan, can you take the follow-up and keep watching for recrudescence?

oncall-ryan: taking handoff. Summary for my notes: reduced prefill workers -> eviction down, streaming_degraded on -> tail latency reduced. Current metrics p95=160ms p99=430ms. Action items: monitor for 30m, gather traces and KV slab allocation histograms, create incident ticket and postmortem. I'll coordinate with applied-ml for workload shaping.

maya: I'll export traces and KV slab allocation dump to the incident ticket (linking here when ready). Also capturing a sample of noisy keys causing churn.

ben: follow-up recommendations: - tune eviction policy to prefer longer-lived prefixes, - cap prefill concurrency in autoscale config, - investigate embedding/search workload causing high churn. Also consider adding a per-tenant cold-pool for heavy streaming clients.

jules: recording action items: (1) root cause deep-dive: fragmentation and churn analysis — maya (2) permanent config change: prefill concurrency cap — ben (3) routing experiment: model-variant under pressure — oncall-ryan (4) postmortem write-up and RCA — jules.

oncall-ryan: marking this thread as handed off. We'll keep pages closed unless the metrics regress. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Incident: "cache-churn -> streaming tail" acknowledged. status=mitigated. Monitoring continues.
